   City Council Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, February 4, 2020

   CALL TO ORDER
   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Harrington

  Harrington, Liao

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. MARCH 2020 ELECTION – VOTER OUTREACH UPDATE
  B. MEASURE SG UPDATE

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council
  on items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council. Pursuant to the Brown Act, the City
  Council cannot answer any questions or take any action until such time as the
  matter may appear as an item on a future agenda.

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be
  aware that all public comments will be limited to a maximum of three minutes.
  You will receive a 30-second warning as you approach the end of your time. As a
  reminder, please be respectful of all speakers regardless of the position they take
  on any items.

  If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a speaker’s request card
  and hand it to the clerk before the start of the meeting. When speaking, please
  state your NAME for the record.

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 4, 2020  2
   1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of January 21, 2020.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of January 21, 2020.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. EXCHANGE OF PROPOSITION A FUNDS

  The City of San Gabriel receives over $800,000 annually in Proposition (Prop)
  A Local Return Funds from Los Angeles County to be used for the benefit of
  public transit. Approximately one-half of the funds are used to operate the
  City’s Dial-A-Ride and Recreation transit programs each year. Since the City
  does not have other eligible projects and must use these funds within a three-
  year period, it has now accumulated a balance of $1 million in unspent Prop
  A Funds. Los Angeles County Metro allows agencies to exchange Prop A
  Funds for General Funds at a discounted rate – a practice that San Gabriel has
  taken advantage of in the past. Foothill Transit has offered to exchange $1
  million of the City’s Prop A Funds for $750,000 in General Funds, representing
  a rate of $.75/$1.00.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the attached Agreement with the Foothill Transit
  Authority authorizing the exchange of $1 million in Proposition A Funds for
  $750,000 in General Funds.

  D. AMENDMENT TO TICKETMASTER USER AGREEMENT

  In 2016, the City of San Gabriel entered into an agreement with Ticketmaster
  LLC for ticketing services for the Mission Playhouse. The initial User
  Agreement had a set term of three years and expired in December 2019.
  Mission Playhouse staff requested an amendment with Ticketmaster LLC
  which renews the term of the agreement and reduces the service fees charged
  to patrons of the Mission Playhouse. The Amendment to the User Agreement
  has a term of five years beginning December 9, 2019 and expiring December

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 4, 2020  3
   9, 2024. This report requests that the City Council ratify the City’s original
  agreement with Ticketmaster and authorize the City Manager to approve the
  Amendment to the User Agreement.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Ratify the Ticketmaster User Agreement from December 2016; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve the Amendment to the User
  Agreement to extend services for an additional five years with the
  amendments to the fee structure.

  E. APPROVAL OF THE SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON FACILITIES
  RELOCATION AGREEMENT (RULE 20B) AND PAYMENT PROCESS FOR
  CURIO HOTEL UTILITY UNDERGROUNDING

  In June 2015, City Council approved a development agreement with Landwin
  DMV, LLC, to provide financial assistance to complete the off-site
  improvements for the 101 West Valley Boulevard Curio Hotel Development
  Project. The required offsite improvements include undergrounding Southern
  California Edison facilities, street widening at Del Mar Avenue, and other
  miscellaneous items. The City would reimburse Developer for the cost of
  constructing the required off-site street improvements by way of paying
  developer a portion of the Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) generated by the
  Hotel Project, per a prior separate agreement.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the Southern California Edison Facilities Relocation Agreement
  and the payment process; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Southern California Edison
  Facilities Relocation Agreement.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. PUBLIC HEARING RESOLUTION NO. 20-07 PROPOSED FY 2020-2021
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROGRAM AND BUDGET
  PLAN

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 4, 2020  4
   The City of San Gabriel receives federal Community Development Block Grant
  (CDBG) funds funded by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban
  Development (HUD) and administered by the Los Angeles County
  Development Authority (LACDA). The funds must be used to meet national
  objectives to develop viable communities and to serve a low- and moderate
  - income population. Use of these federal funds also requires compliance with
  statutory requirements including financial, environmental review,
  procurement, construction, eligibility, reporting, and citizen participation. The
  proposed Fiscal Year 2020-21 CDBG Program budget funding request totals
  $358,594.

  Recommended Action:

  The Community Development Department recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt the attached Resolution No. 20-07 authorizing the allocation of
  CDBG funds for FY 2020-21 from the LACDA for activities and projects
  described above and in Exhibit A of the Resolution.

  2. Carry over any CDBG funds unspent at the close of FY 2019-20 and
  recognize the receipt of FY 2020-21 CDBG Program funds awarded by the
  LACDA to the City FY 2020-21 Budget.

  3. Recognize the receipt of an estimated $20,630 of CDBG funds from
  Supervisor Barger, if funds are approved by the Board of Supervisors for
  the After-School Program.

  4. Approve appropriating $52,034 of previous years’ CDBG unallocated funds
  to FY 2020-21 program and budget.

  5. Allocate any FY 2020-21 CDBG funds in excess of estimated funds to the
  Street Improvement Project and/or the Youth Services Program.

  6. Authorize the City Manager to execute new contracts with the LACDA for
  the allocation of FY 2020-21 CDBG Program and make adjustments as
  necessary to reflect the actual allocation of funds to San Gabriel.

 6. NEW BUSINESS – None.

 7. PUBLIC COMMENT

 8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 4, 2020  5
  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 11. ADJOURNMENT

  The next Regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, February 18, 2020
  at 6:30 p.m. in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
  Gabriel, California. Information regarding matters to be considered at each
  meeting will be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the
  City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.
